I made GHZ states of 2, 3, 4, and 5 qubits on the real IQM computer sirius. All four circuits ran as one job, with 100 shots each. Before that, I ran the same job on the free test device sirius:mock (job 01a1604c-b50d-745a-b275-536f7d289268). It completed, but the test device always returns all zeros. That run only proved the job was set up correctly. The real job is 01a1604c-f394-71a0-92ac-afd754feec0d. The API reports 1.0 billed second for it. At the sirius rate of 0.3 credits per second, that is about 0.3 credits. That figure is an estimate.

In a GHZ state, all the qubits are linked together. When you measure them, they should all give 0 or all give 1, about half the time each. A perfect machine would give a matching result on 100% of shots. Here is how often all the bits matched on sirius:
- 2 qubits: 95 of 100 shots (0.95)
- 3 qubits: 89 of 100 shots (0.89)
- 4 qubits: 84 of 100 shots (0.84)
- 5 qubits: 84 of 100 shots (0.84)

The trend is that bigger GHZ states lose more to noise. Each extra qubit adds one more two-qubit gate. On sirius, qubits connect through a shared central resonator, so each extra qubit also adds two more MOVE operations. Every gate, every MOVE, and every measurement has a small chance of error. One error anywhere can flip a single bit, and then that shot no longer matches. The bad shots show this, because most of them have exactly one bit flipped, such as 01111 or 00001. The 4-qubit and 5-qubit results are equal at 0.84. With 100 shots, each fraction is uncertain by about 4 percentage points, so the small step from 4 to 5 qubits is hidden in that noise. The general rule is that entanglement gets more fragile as it spreads over more qubits, because the chances of error add up. The zeros and ones were also not exactly 50/50, for example 46 to 38 at 5 qubits. That is partly chance in 100 shots and partly readout bias.

My script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_664c303a-347-232/ghz_run.py. It saved the results in the same folder as result_sirius.json and result_sirius_mock.json.
